summary: This study fabricated Ti3C2Tx MXene-infiltrated porous silica (MX-PS) electrodes by LiF/HCl MILD synthesis of MXene, camphene-based unidirectional freeze casting of silica, and capillary-driven infiltration. The electrochemical electrode variants differed by MXene dispersion concentration (90 versus 180 mg mL−1), silica-backbone porosity (40% versus 60%), and pore orientation (longitudinal versus lateral); a non-infiltrated porous-silica device was also fabricated as a reference. The primary 60%-porosity longitudinal MX-PS electrode made with 180 mg mL−1 dispersion delivered 7.24 F cm−2 and 7.26 F g−1 at 10 mV s−1, with 2.43 mg cm−2 MXene loading. Several variant capacitances were displayed only graphically, so numerical values, variant-specific loadings, SSA, tortuosity, and interlayer spacings were not reported in the supplied text.
